test_title: PYST 62: SSC CPO - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: In a class, there are 60 students. The average weight of the entire class is 42 kg. If there are 36 boys in the class and the average weight of all the boys is 50 kg, then what is the average weight (in kg) of all the girls?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Boys** to **Girls** = 36 : (60 − 36) = 36 : 24 = 3 : 2

Using the **Alligation Method**: Average weight of Boys is 50 kg and the Class Average is 42 kg.

Difference between **Boys Average** and **Class Average** = 50 − 42 = 8 units.

This difference of 8 corresponds to the **Girls ratio part** (2 units) ⇒ 2 units = 8 ⇒ 1 unit = 4.

The **Boys ratio part** is 3 units, which corresponds to 3 × 4 = 12.

Average weight of Girls = Class Average − 12 = 42 − 12 = 30 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total students = 60

Average weight of entire class = 42 kg

Number of boys = 36

Average weight of boys = 50 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ab1ae7ab3cb6715907409ddca17a5bb34ec1a3cd88b33a427a3b0408128836e.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Average Weight = Total Weight ÷ Total Number of Students

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of the class = 60 × 42 = 2520 kg

⇒ Total weight of the boys = 36 × 50 = 1800 kg

⇒ Number of girls = 60 − 36 = 24

⇒ Total weight of the girls = Total weight of class − Total weight of boys

⇒ Total weight of the girls = 2520 − 1800 = 720 kg

⇒ Average weight of the girls = 720 ÷ 24

⇒ Average weight of the girls = 30 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 30 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

The average of two groups combined is given by (n₁×A₁ + n₂×A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the quantity and A is the average.

Alligation Rule

Quantity of cheaper / Quantity of dearer = (Rate of dearer − Mean rate) / (Mean rate − Rate of cheaper).

Deviation Method

Assume a base average and calculate the net deviation. The sum of deviations from the actual mean is always zero.</p
